plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: Leafless stalks shoot up almost overnight from bare ground. Each one is topped with a crown of crimson flowers whose curling petals and long, arching stamens look like fine filaments of fire. Whole rice-field edges, riverbanks and temple grounds turn scarlet around the autumn equinox.
plants.bloomingSeason: September, around the autumn equinox (peaking mid to late September)
plants.location: Japan, especially Saitama Prefecture and rural rice-field edges and riverbanks
plants.funFact: The flowers appear without any leaves. The foliage emerges only after the blooms fade and lasts through winter, which is the reverse of most bulbs. In Japan the flower is traditionally linked to the equinox holiday, called Higan.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped blooms push straight out of the soil as the garden winds down for the year. They look like pale lilac crocuses, with no leaves to accompany them. Clusters of flowers emerge from each corm, and they brighten lawns, meadows and borders just as the autumn chill sets in.
plants.location: Temperate meadows and gardens of Europe and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true crocus. It belongs to the lily family and contains colchicine, a potent toxin that has also been used in plant breeding and in medicine.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family looks like a flower crowned with a halo. It has a bowl of silky, pink-tipped central bracts surrounded by rows of rosy, petal-like bracts. It stands boldly above leathery evergreen foliage on the mountain slopes of the Cape, and it is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter through spring, with the season running from about July to October in its native range
plants.location: Fynbos mountain slopes of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It grows from a thick underground stem called a lignotuber. This lets the plant resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep through the fynbos.
